name: BACH_0085
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (90%)** · Confident · Careful review
Single-class conformal set, invasive probability 0%; MUSK disagrees.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 90%, Normal 9% | Clear lead |
| Conformal set | Benign only | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.98 / 88th percentile | Input not flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Different top class |
| Similar cases | 3 of 5 Benign [F5] | Moderate support |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 3) · ↓ invasive · Scores below typical; lowers invasive association [F2] · Validated
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 4, 5, 8) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; linked to lower invasive likelihood [F3] · Weak
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (regions 0, 8) · ↓ invasive · Scores high; modest link to lower invasive likelihood · Validated
- **Tumor cell fraction** (regions 3, 9, 11) · context · 66% of sampled nuclei neoplastic, 96th percentile [F7] · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Top-3 removal drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI (−0.005 to 0.007) includes 0; not shown to reflect the classifier. Mitoses, normal lobules, necrosis are Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- MUSK picks a different top class, so the Benign call may not hold.
- Sampled nuclei show a 96th-percentile tumor fraction, uneasy for a Benign call.

## Check on slide
1. **Regions 3, 9, 11**: Check whether cells called neoplastic are truly atypical.
2. **Region 3**: Look for stromal invasion; the concept scores low even here.
3. **Regions 4, 5, 8**: Confirm gland or tubule architecture supporting the benign reading.
